description: Attestation and trust-profile test vectors for InsumerAPI wallet state, each paired with the result a correct verifier must produce. Twelve entries are issuer responses exactly as issued (01 to 07, 12, 13, 17, 18, 26). The other fifteen are derived from those: fourteen carry a deliberate edit to the signed bytes or their labelling (08, 09, 10, 11, 14, 15, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 27), and 16 is byte-identical to 01 and differs only in the verifier options it is presented under. The derived entries must be refused or reported as unverifiable, as each expected block states.

verified_with.note: The published verdicts were produced by the issuer's own reference verifier against the issuer's stated expectations. They are not an independent confirmation. Everything needed to write an independent verifier and disagree is in this file and in the repository.
verified_with.version_note: These are the exact versions the published verdicts were produced under, pinned in vectors/package.json with a lockfile and installed with npm ci. They record what ran rather than a minimum requirement; the reference-implementation floor stated elsewhere in this file is a separate claim.
verified_with.jwks_note: Sixteen entries (11 to 22 and 24 to 27) resolve their keys from the live JWKS when they run; the other eleven verify against the key built into insumer-verify and fetch nothing. The snapshot above is the key set these verdicts were produced against, for reproducing them after a key rotation.

note: This file is a discovery copy. The repository above carries the same vectors plus a runner, and is the authority if the two ever differ.

contract.canonicalization: JSON with keys sorted lexicographically and recursively, no whitespace, standard separators
contract.hash_algorithm: SHA-256, rendered as a 0x-prefixed lowercase hex string
contract.signature_algorithm: ECDSA P-256 (ES256), raw P1363 encoding, base64
contract.signature_preimage_v1: insertion-order JSON of {id, pass, results, attestedAt}, no domain tag
contract.scheme_selection: The kid on each response selects both the key and the signing scheme. A verifier MUST branch on it and MUST NOT assume a single scheme. Every key created on or after the v2 rollout is v2.
contract.reference_implementation: insumer-verify@1.9.2 or later (npm); vectors 01 to 10, 12 to 18 and 20 to 23 also match under 1.8.4 to 1.9.1, vectors 24 and 25 need 1.8.6, vectors 26 and 27 need 1.8.7, and vectors 11 and 19 need 1.9.2, which reports each check on its own when the kid selects no key
contract.specification_sections: Signing in section 3.3.1, result fields in 5.2, condition hashes in 8, anchoring in 9, verification algorithm in 12, scheme versioning in 14
contract.pq_signature_algorithm: ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204), pure, empty context; RFC 9964 JWK (kty AKP, alg ML-DSA-65, pub) in the same JWKS, kid insumer-attest-pq1 (attest) / insumer-trust-pq1 (trust), appended after the EC entries
contract.pq_signature_preimage: "insumer.attestation.pq1" + "\n" + <the exact classical preimage the classical kid selects: v1 bare JSON.stringify({id,pass,results,attestedAt}) or the v2 domain-tagged canonical JSON>; trust profiles use "insumer.trust.pq1"
contract.pq_fields: data.pqSig (base64, 3309 bytes) + data.pqKid beside data.sig/data.kid; JWT format additionally carries data.pqJwt, a compact JWS (alg ML-DSA-65) over the same claims as data.jwt, bound to it by the full claim set: the same member names and, for every member, a deeply equal value, compared as parsed JSON and never by bytes (insumer-verify 1.8.6 or later; earlier releases compared jti, exp and pass)
contract.pq_key_binding: https://insumermodel.com/.well-known/pq-key-binding.json (content-addressed, PQ-self-signed, classically cross-signed, anchored on Base tx 0x30a10ccd49547c4bd9ebb47adce5d3470e4760ab456753d743597ebce6a455e6, block 50758053, 2026-09-01T23:30:53Z)

inputs: results[].evaluatedCondition, the exact predicate that was applied
results[].conditionHash, the claimed digest of its canonical form
the chain anchor on each result: an EVM block or an XRPL ledger names the state that was read, a Solana slot is a floor, and Bitcoin, Tron, Stellar and Sui anchors are tip markers
data.pqSig and data.pqKid (or data.pqJwt), when present
data.jwt and data.pqJwt, when the response carries them beside data.attestation
recomputation_procedure.harness: insumer-verify@1.9.2 or later, or any implementation of the contract above
steps: Select the key from the JWKS by kid. A kid matching no key is a failure, not a reason to fall back to another key. A kid this verifier does not recognise also selects no signing scheme, so it selects no preimage: the post-quantum companion is then unverifiable, never refuted, and no other era's preimage may be substituted for it. A recognised kid naming the other artifact type is a relabelled artifact and is refuted (vector 21). A kid that selects no key fails the signature verdict alone: the remaining steps need no key and are still performed and reported as their own verdicts, and a companion that was not transmitted is absent (vectors 11 and 19).
Rebuild the signed preimage for the scheme that kid names and verify the ECDSA P-256 signature over its SHA-256.
For each result, canonicalize evaluatedCondition, take the SHA-256, and compare to conditionHash.
Compare blockTimestamp against a caller-defined maximum age, if one is set.
Compare expiresAt against the current time.

Resolve pqKid to the AKP key in the JWKS (unresolvable = unverifiable, never a pass). Verify the ML-DSA-65 signature in pqSig over the pq domain tag + the classical preimage rebuilt in step 2. Report the companion as its own verdict: verified, refuted, absent, or unverifiable. Refuted always fails; absent or unverifiable fail only under the verifier's own pqRequiredFrom cutoff, judged by the verifier's clock, and never when reading an artifact as evidence.

In the JWT format the companion is data.pqJwt, not pqSig: verify that compact JWS (alg ML-DSA-65, the AKP key its kid names) over its own header.payload bytes, then confirm its payload and the ES256 jwt's payload carry the identical claim set, the same member names and deeply equal values, compared as parsed JSON and never by bytes. Any difference is refuted (vectors 24 and 25). The verdict and the cutoff rule are those of the previous step.

When a response carries data.jwt beside data.attestation (what format: "jwt" returns), verify the tokens too and report them as their own verdict: the ES256 signature of jwt under the same kid as the response, its condition hashes as in step 3, that it is the token of this attestation (jti equals id; pass, results and exp equal the attestation's pass, results and expiresAt in whole seconds), and its pqJwt as in the previous step. A failure fails the artifact (vector 27). The signed attestation does not name the wallet; the jwt does, so a jwt that is read must have been verified.
recomputation_procedure.expected_output_form: Five independent verdicts, reported separately rather than collapsed into one boolean: signature, conditionHashes, freshness, expiry, pq (status verified | refuted | absent | unverifiable); and a sixth, jwt, only when the response carries tokens beside the attestation.
recomputation_procedure.boundary: This procedure establishes that the issuer hashed and signed exactly the predicate it says it evaluated, bound to a named point in chain history. It does not re-run the chain read. That is the verifying party's own work, and the anchor plus the evaluated predicate are the two inputs needed to do it against any node. The read goes against public chain state rather than against anything the issuer holds.

expiry_note: Every vector in this file is past its freshness window, so a correct run reports expiry as failed for all of them. That is expected and is stated in each expected block. An attestation records that a wallet met a condition at a named block, and that does not decay. The expiry timestamp is a freshness policy for access decisions, not a statement about whether the verdict is correct. Because insumer-verify derives its top-level valid as the AND of all its checks, valid is false for every vector here; the per-check breakdown is what these vectors assert.

anchor_fields.note: The anchor field differs by chain family. A verifier that assumes blockNumber finds no anchor on a Bitcoin result.

wallets.0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA960: vitalik.eth, the address used throughout the InsumerAPI examples
wallets.0xAd982CB19aCCa2923Df8F687C0614a7700255a: The wallet profiled by the trust vectors (18 and 21). A public Ethereum address; a trust profile carries booleans and counts, never balances.

01-token-balance-met.description: A token_balance condition the wallet meets: USDC on Ethereum mainnet, gte 1.
01-token-balance-met.note: Held more than the threshold at the anchored block. Re-derived from chain state before publication.

02-token-balance-not-met.description: The same condition with a threshold the wallet does not meet: USDC gte 1000.
02-token-balance-not-met.note: A signed false is a verdict, not an error. Thresholds are token/display units, so 1000 means 1000 USDC.

03-token-balance-dai.description: An 18-decimal token: DAI on Ethereum mainnet, gte 1.
03-token-balance-dai.note: A different decimal scale from vector 01, an 18-decimal token rather than 6.

04-token-balance-weth.description: A second 18-decimal token: WETH on Ethereum mainnet, gte 1.
04-token-balance-weth.note: An 18-decimal token, met at the anchored block.

05-multi-condition-mixed.description: Two conditions in one attestation, one met and one not.
05-multi-condition-mixed.note: Top-level pass is the AND across results, so it is false while results[0].met is true. Each result carries its own evaluatedCondition, conditionHash and anchor.

06-second-chain-base.description: The same condition type on a second EVM chain: USDC on Base, gte 1.
06-second-chain-base.note: Anchoring is per result, so a multi-chain attestation carries a different block per chain.

07-non-evm-anchor-bitcoin.description: A non-EVM chain: native BTC, gte 1, on the Bitcoin genesis address.
07-non-evm-anchor-bitcoin.note: The anchor is blockHeight and blockHash, not blockNumber, and chainId is the string "bitcoin" rather than a number. A verifier that assumes blockNumber will find no anchor here. Verified independently: the blockHash matches the block at that height, and the balance at that block met the threshold. The anchor itself is a tip marker: it binds the observation to a recent block and does not name the state that was read.

08-tampered-condition.description: Vector 01 with the signed threshold rewritten from "1" to "0.000001".
08-tampered-condition.note: Both fail, for different reasons: the hash no longer matches the condition, and the condition sits inside the signed payload. The recompute block below shows reproduces:false.

09-tampered-signature.description: Vector 01 with the first character of the signature altered.
09-tampered-signature.note: The condition hash still reproduces, because the condition was untouched. This is the vector that proves a verifier reports signature failure and hash integrity independently rather than collapsing them into one boolean.

10-tampered-condition-hash.description: Vector 01 with the claimed conditionHash replaced, the condition itself left alone.
10-tampered-condition-hash.note: The inverse of vector 08. The hash is inside the signed payload, so editing it breaks the signature as well as failing recomputation.

11-unresolvable-kid.description: Vector 01 presented with a kid that resolves to no key in the JWKS.
11-unresolvable-kid.note: Must fail closed. A verifier that falls back to the first key in the document verifies an unknown or forged kid against whichever key is listed first. insumer-verify has refused this from 1.7.0; earlier versions fell back. Needs the jwksUrl option, since key resolution is only exercised when a JWKS is fetched. A kid that resolves to no key in the set fails the signature verdict alone, with a reason naming the kid it could not place. The other verdicts need no key and are reported on their own: the condition hashes are recomputed and reproduce (the recompute block below), freshness and expiry report their own results, and the companion is absent because none was transmitted, exactly as on vector 23. insumer-verify 1.9.2 and later report it this way; 1.7.0 to 1.9.1 reported every check failed and the companion unverifiable once the kid failed to resolve.

12-pq-companion-v2.description: A v2 attestation carrying the post-quantum companion (pqSig, pqKid) as issued.
12-pq-companion-v2.note: Real response, signed by the production ES256 key and the production ML-DSA-65 key. The pqSig companion signs "insumer.attestation.pq1" + "\n" + the exact classical preimage the classical kid selects (ML-DSA-65, FIPS 204; key insumer-attest-pq1 in the JWKS as an RFC 9964 AKP entry). It is reported as a fifth verdict, pq, beside the four classical checks; a refuted companion always fails, an absent or unverifiable one fails only under the verifier's own pqRequiredFrom policy. Expected pq status: verified.

13-pq-companion-v1.description: A v1 (frozen bare-JSON scheme) attestation carrying the same post-quantum companion.
13-pq-companion-v1.note: Shows the companion covers the v1 era unchanged: pqSig is over the pq domain tag + the v1 bare JSON.stringify preimage. Real response, v1 key. Expected pq status: verified.

14-pq-companion-tampered.description: Vector 12 with one byte of pqSig altered.
14-pq-companion-tampered.note: The classical signature still verifies (it was not touched); the companion is REFUTED, and a refuted companion fails the artifact regardless of policy or mode. Expected pq status: refuted.

15-pq-kid-unresolvable.description: Vector 12 presented with a pqKid that resolves to no key in the JWKS, under a verifier that requires the companion.
15-pq-kid-unresolvable.note: Could-not-check is never a pass: the companion is UNVERIFIABLE. With pqRequiredFrom set to a past date (a live access decision after the verifier's own cutoff), unverifiable fails the artifact; without pqRequiredFrom it would be reported and not fail. Expected pq status: unverifiable.

16-pq-absent-under-cutoff.description: Vector 01 (issued before post-quantum signing existed) presented to a verifier whose cutoff has passed.
16-pq-absent-under-cutoff.note: In access mode past pqRequiredFrom, an absent companion fails the artifact: this is the cutoff working. In evidence mode (mode: "evidence") the same artifact is never refused; the verifier reports pq absent and, given pqActivatedAt = the anchored binding date 2026-09-01T23:30:53Z, existedAtIssuance: false. Expected pq status: absent.

17-pq-jwt-companion.description: The JWT-format envelope: the ES256 jwt with its ML-DSA-65 sibling pqJwt.
17-pq-jwt-companion.note: pqJwt is a separate compact JWS (alg ML-DSA-65, kid insumer-attest-pq1) over the same claims as jwt; the verifier binds it to jwt by the full claim set (same member names, deeply equal values, compared as parsed JSON and never by bytes), so the companion vouches for every claim read from jwt and cannot be transplanted from another artifact; vectors 24 and 25 are the refused cases. Handing the envelope object {data:{jwt,pqJwt}} to verifyAttestation routes to the JWT path. Expected pq status: verified.

18-trust-profile-not-evaluated.description: A real trust profile from POST /v1/trust with only the EVM wallet supplied, so the checks that need a Solana, XRPL, Stellar or Sui wallet carry the not-evaluated marker.
18-trust-profile-not-evaluated.note: Real response, signed by the production ES256 key under kid insumer-trust-v2 (preimage "insumer.trust.v2" + "\n" + the canonical JSON of the whole trust object, expiresAt inside it, no v member) and by the production ML-DSA-65 key under pqKid insumer-trust-pq1. Six checks in institutional_stablecoins could not be run because the wallet their chain needs was not supplied: each carries evaluated: false, reason wallet_not_provided, requires naming the request parameter that would let it run, met: false, and no chain anchor. They are counted in notEvaluatedCount on the dimension and totalNotEvaluated in the summary, never in passCount, failCount, totalPassed or totalFailed (specification 11.3). An unevaluated check is not a failure. It is a check the issuer states, inside the signed profile, that it did not run; a verifier treats it as neither met nor failed, and a freshness check skips it because there is no anchor to age. The marker is signed content: removing it, or rewriting the counts, breaks the signature. The recompute block covers every check in the profile; the six marker checks are the ones with anchor null. Expected pq status: verified.

19-missing-kid.description: Vector 13 presented with its kid removed.
19-missing-kid.note: Must fail. A response with no kid selects neither a key nor a signing scheme. A verifier that fills the gap, whether with the first key in the JWKS, a positional default, or its own built-in key, checks the artifact against a key the response never named and reports a signature it had no basis to verify. This vector is derived from the v1-signed vector 13 rather than from vector 01 because that is the case a fallback accepts: a v1 artifact verifies under the frozen bare-JSON scheme against the shared EC key, so a verifier that defaults to that scheme and to any available key reports it valid, companion and all. insumer-verify 1.8.0 and 1.8.1 do exactly that; 1.8.2 and later refuse a missing kid on every input path. jwksUrl is pinned so that key selection is the step that fails: with no kid there is nothing to select by. That fails the signature verdict alone, with a reason saying the response carries no kid. The other verdicts need no key and are reported on their own: the condition hashes are recomputed and reproduce (the recompute block below), and freshness and expiry report their own results. The companion was transmitted, but with no kid there is no preimage to rebuild it over, so it is unverifiable, never refuted; without a pqRequiredFrom cutoff that is reported and not refused, as on vector 22. insumer-verify 1.9.2 and later report it this way; 1.8.2 to 1.9.1 reported every check failed once the kid was missing.

20-attest-under-trust-kid.description: Vector 01 presented under insumer-trust-v2, the kid that signs trust profiles.
20-attest-under-trust-kid.note: Must fail. The kid resolves: insumer-trust-v2 is in the JWKS, and it names the same EC coordinates as insumer-attest-v2. What it does not do is sign attestations. A kid is bound to its artifact type as well as to a key and a scheme (attestations verify under insumer-attest-v1 or insumer-attest-v2, trust profiles under insumer-attest-v1 or insumer-trust-v2), and a verifier that resolves the key and stops there accepts an attestation relabelled as a trust profile, or the reverse, whenever the two kids share a key, which today they do. insumer-verify checks the binding from 1.8.2 onward. jwksUrl is pinned so that key resolution succeeds and the refusal is shown to come from the binding, not from a lookup failure. Vector 21 is the same mislabelling in the other direction.

21-trust-under-attest-kid.description: Vector 18 presented under insumer-attest-v2, the kid that signs attestations.
21-trust-under-attest-kid.note: Must fail. The reverse of vector 20: a genuine trust profile relabelled with the attestation kid. The kid resolves to the same EC key, so a verifier that only resolves keys verifies nothing wrong and reports the signature valid; one that binds kids to artifact types refuses it. The companion verdict follows the classical kid, because the companion signs the exact classical preimage the classical kid selects: with the kid rewritten there is no correct preimage to rebuild, so the untouched pqSig cannot verify against anything, and insumer-verify 1.8.3 reports it refuted. The artifact fails on the classical signature regardless of how the companion is reported. Expected pq status: refuted.

22-pq-kid-other-artifact.description: Vector 12 presented with its pqKid changed to insumer-trust-pq1, the companion kid for trust profiles.
22-pq-kid-other-artifact.note: The classical checks pass: sig and kid are untouched. The companion kid resolves, since insumer-trust-pq1 is in the JWKS as an AKP entry over the same ML-DSA-65 key as insumer-attest-pq1, but it names the other artifact type, so the companion is UNVERIFIABLE: a known kid that does not belong to this artifact is a mislabelled companion, not evidence for or against the signature, and it is never re-interpreted under the kid the verifier would have expected. No pqRequiredFrom is pinned, so the artifact is not refused for it; under a cutoff that has passed it would be, exactly as vector 15. Expected pq status: unverifiable.

23-unknown-kid-no-jwks.description: Vector 01 presented with a kid that names no published key, to a verifier that has not been given a JWKS URL.
23-unknown-kid-no-jwks.note: Vector 11 shows an unknown kid failing when the verifier fetches the JWKS. This vector removes the fetch: no jwksUrl is pinned, so insumer-verify falls back to its built-in InsumerAPI key. A kid the verifier cannot place must still fail, and must fail as could-not-verify rather than as forged: nothing about the signature has been shown wrong, the verifier simply has no key or scheme it is entitled to check it under. It must never be resolved by using whatever key is at hand. insumer-verify reports the signature verdict failed with a reason that names the kid it could not place; the reason is the classical verdict's only carrier of the unverifiable-versus-refuted distinction, since the classical checks report a boolean and a reason rather than a status. The condition hashes still reproduce and the companion is absent, as on vector 01.

24-pq-jwt-subject-differs.description: The JWT-format envelope of vector 17 with the jwt's sub claim edited; the pqJwt beside it is untouched and genuine.
24-pq-jwt-subject-differs.note: Derived from vector 17. Only the sub claim inside jwt was changed (to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD); the ES256 signature segment and the whole pqJwt are byte-identical to vector 17. The ES256 signature no longer verifies, and the companion is refuted as well: a pqJwt is bound to its jwt by the full claim set (same member names, deeply equal values), so a genuine companion does not vouch for a jwt whose subject differs from the one it signed. Requires insumer-verify 1.8.6 or later for the pq verdict; earlier releases compared jti, exp and pass only.

25-pq-jwt-results-differ.description: The JWT-format envelope of vector 17 with results[0].met inverted inside the jwt; the pqJwt beside it is untouched and genuine.
25-pq-jwt-results-differ.note: Derived from vector 17. Only results[0].met inside jwt was inverted; pass, jti, exp and sub are unchanged, and the ES256 signature segment and the whole pqJwt are byte-identical to vector 17. The condition hash still reproduces, because it covers the evaluated condition and not the verdict. The ES256 signature no longer verifies, and the companion is refuted: the full claim set is bound, so the per-condition results a relying party reads from the jwt must be the ones the companion signed. Requires insumer-verify 1.8.6 or later for the pq verdict; earlier releases compared jti, exp and pass only.

26-jwt-format-whole-response.description: A format: "jwt" response exactly as the API returned it: the attestation with sig, kid, pqSig and pqKid, and beside it the ES256 jwt and its ML-DSA-65 sibling pqJwt.
26-jwt-format-whole-response.note: Issued 2026-09-20 under an insumer-attest-v2 key, saved verbatim. Vector 17 carries the two tokens alone; this is the whole object a caller actually receives. A verifier given it verifies the attestation and its companion, and the tokens as well, reported as checks.jwt: the ES256 signature of jwt under the same kid, its condition hashes, that it is the token of this attestation (jti, pass, results and exp equal the attestation's), and the pqJwt companion over the full claim set. Requires insumer-verify 1.8.7 or later for the jwt verdict; earlier releases verify the attestation and report nothing about the tokens.

27-jwt-format-token-edited.description: Vector 26 with the sub claim edited inside data.jwt. The attestation, its signature, its companion and the pqJwt are untouched.
27-jwt-format-token-edited.note: Derived from vector 26. Only the sub claim inside data.jwt was changed (to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD); every other byte of the response is as issued. The attestation still verifies, and its companion still verifies, because neither was touched and neither names the wallet. The response must be refused all the same, at checks.jwt: the wallet is read from the jwt, and the jwt in this response no longer carries a valid signature. A verifier that checks the attestation and stops reports this response valid. Requires insumer-verify 1.8.7 or later.

pq_note: Vectors 01 to 11 carry no companion: 01 to 07 were issued before post-quantum signing existed (2026-08-28), and 08 to 11 derive from vector 01. For all of them a correct run reports pq as absent, which does not fail them unless the runner sets pqRequiredFrom. Vector 16 is vector 01 re-presented under a cutoff, so it carries no companion either. Vectors 12, 13 and 17 are issuer responses from after the anchored binding (2026-09-01T23:30:53Z) and carry the companion as issued; 14 and 15 derive from 12 by altering the companion or its kid. Reading any artifact after the fact is evidence mode: nothing is refused for lacking a companion; the anchored binding date tells the reader whether one could have existed. Vectors 18-23 (added 2026-09-02) cover the trust-profile not-evaluated marker (spec 11.3) and the kid rules a verifier applies since insumer-verify 1.8.2: a missing kid fails, a kid selects only the artifact type it is bound to, an unknown kid with no JWKS supplied is unverifiable rather than refuted, and a pqKid of the other artifact type leaves the companion unverifiable while the classical checks stand. Checks the profile could not evaluate carry evaluated: false and are counted in notEvaluatedCount and totalNotEvaluated, never as failures. Vectors 24 and 25 (added 2026-09-20) derive from vector 17 by editing one claim inside jwt (sub on 24, results[0].met on 25) and leaving the pqJwt untouched: in the JWT format the companion binds the full claim set, so a genuine pqJwt beside a jwt whose claims differ is refuted. They need insumer-verify 1.8.6 or later for that verdict. Vectors 26 and 27 (added 2026-09-20) are a whole format: "jwt" response, as issued and with the sub claim edited inside data.jwt: the tokens beside an attestation are verified and bound to it, and reported as checks.jwt (insumer-verify 1.8.7 or later).
